recipes.name: Simple Hush Puppies
ingredients_raw: 1 quart vegetable oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk milk, egg, and onion together in a bowl. Stir pancake mix, cornmeal, and salt into milk mixture to form a smooth batter.

Scoop ping pong ball-sized balls of batter using a small ice cream scoop; drop about 5 scoops per batch into the hot oil. Fry until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Remove hush puppies with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Repeat with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Hush Puppies
raw_recipe.description: These hush puppies are quick and easy to prepare, using pancake mix and cornmeal for the batter. They will surely please all of your guests.

review.reviewBody: My young girl loved these i added a little bit of cooked sausage to the center before adding them to the oil.
I added 1 tsp of garlic powder. Easy and tasty hush puppies. My first time making hush puppies. My husband gave rave reviews.

I added more onion. They were great, baked up light and fluffy but I need more flavor. The next batch I added 2T Tony Chachere's and 1T salt. That was a grave error, way too much salt and I'm a salt fiend. Don't do that. Lol
I thought the batter was a tad bit bland so I added 1/4 cup of sugar and what a difference it made.
This is a very easy cheap recipe! I made it when my grandparents came over for a fish fry. And it’s very good if you do 3/4 cups of buttermilk instead of 3/4 cups of milk. 🤫 🐶 Hush—-puppies

Love this recipe! It is simple to make AND tasty!! I use a SMIDGE of garlic powder & fresh frozen minced onion. (I chop up the extra oinion & freeze it on a tray. Then once frozen put it in a zipper lock bag to use as needed for this, spaghetti, salads.. ) since the onion is fresh & not dehydrated I use about 1/2 again as much.

I liked that these used baking mix for a quick shortcut instead of finding and measuring out all the components. I added some green chives too, as I remembered hush puppies always have something green in them and I wasn't sure if it were parsley, onion, or something else, so I added some chives in, sticking with the onion theme. I think I should have used much more onion as these didn't have much flavor. My husband said the same thing, they are kind of bland and need more. He thought maybe a pinch of cayenne would help. I think it simply needs more onion. The directions were very clear and these cooked up beautifully. They felt a little heavy and dense, but I am not certain how to tweak that. Maybe less cornmeal, or using a self rising corn flour? Of course, I might have overmixed the dough causing it myself. I'd like to try these again, adding more onion, something green for color and more onion pop, and maybe or maybe not some cayenne pepper too.

The texture of these makes for the best hushpuppy I've ever had. I agree with previous reviewers though that they are pretty bland as written, thus the 4 stars instead of 5. I added some canned green chilies and some Cajun seasoning and now they are spectacular. I served them with Charleton Crab and Grits from this site and they were quite popular.

Quick and easy. Light and moist yet crispy with a sweet corn flavor. Had both pancake and pie crust mixes on hand but used the pancake. Also used a very fine corn flour and diced red onion. Made these to serve with jambalaya. Great pairing for Cajun dishes. Thanks for this recipe.

Minced green onions are pretty yummy in these. I like to add extra baking powder to make them lighter. My grandma made hush puppies with the leftover milk & breading mixtures, I need to experiment with that until I get it right. Also, Tony Chachere's is the way to go here. It needs some spicy in there. I add several healthy shakes of Crystal hot sauce to the milk mixture. A Louisiana girl has to have her spicy on!
I added some crushed red pepper. I think I over cooked them b/c they were tough.
Easy to read , no additions
Added jalapeños and some red pepper flakes cause I like a little kick. Easy. Very goo
